definition: Measurement theory is the set of ideas and methods used to examine whether an assessment actually measures the underlying trait it is intended to measure. In this context, it focuses on issues such as dimensionality and whether the items reflect one common latent variable, because scores are hard to interpret if the instrument is not measuring the intended construct.

reasons: The packet does not support the general claim that “Measurement theory is the set of ideas and methods used” to check whether an assessment measures an intended trait; it only describes using Rasch measurement theory and discusses assessing dimensionality/unidimensionality.

The definition refers broadly to “latent variable” and “intended construct” and total-score interpretability; while the packet supports the importance of dimensionality/unidimensionality and that total scores may be invalid if the instrument is not measuring what it is supposed to, it does not clearly ground the broader, field-spanning wording used in the definition.

The packet frames the method as “Rasch measurement theory,” but the definition uses “measurement theory” without demonstrating that this exact term (as opposed to Rasch measurement theory) is defined in the packet in the way stated.
